correctness.rationale: A label-1 vertex would need an adjacent positive defender and therefore violate independent positive support. The support is consequently an independent dominating set. If t is the greatest index of a positive B-vertex, domination forces every B-index at most t and every A-index greater than t into the support, yielding the unique canonical cut support S_t. The leaf or cut-boundary zero vertices force the displayed label-3 vertices, which then defend every zero; all remaining support labels are independently 2 or 3. The standalone checker directly evaluates all quaternary labelings for n=2 through 5 and matches the classification and coefficient histogram.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete all-function enumeration for an established domination variant on the canonical twin-free chain family. The cut-support theorem is the natural structural core, the closed polynomial supplies every weight multiplicity, and the minimum value and its two optimizers follow as immediate consequences.
